DELETE /Playlists/{playlistId}/Users/{us.classification: jellyfin-bug: Jellyfin's DELETE is a silent no-op on BOTH v10.11.8 and master. `PlaylistsController.RemoveUserFromPlaylist` (identical in both trees) resolves the share from one Playlist instance, then `PlaylistManager.RemoveUserFromShares` (v10.11.8 L641-648 / master L669-676, byte-identical) re-fetches a DIFFERENT instance via GetPlaylistForUser -> GetPlaylists -> LibraryManager.GetItemList (master L1656-1673, which returns _itemRepository.GetItemList directly, bypassing the BaseItem cache and materialising fresh objects) and calls `shares.Remove(share)`. `MediaBrowser.Model/Entities/PlaylistUserPermissions.cs:8` is a plain class with only UserId/CanEdit auto-properties — no Equals, no IEquatable, not a record — so `EqualityComparer<T>.Default` is REFERENCE equality, Remove returns false, the UNCHANGED list is written back, and the controller returns 204. Corroborated inside the same file: `AddUserToShares` removes an element it took from the SAME list, which is why POST works and DELETE does not. `git log v10.11.8..master` over both paths contains no change to RemoveUserFromShares — MASTER HAS NOT FIXED THIS. Ferrofin deletes by (playlist_id, user_id) in SQL (ferrofin-core/src/collection_manager.rs `remove_user_from_shares`), which is the semantic intent of the C#, so the share actually goes and a repeat DELETE correctly 404s — the controller's own `share is null -> NotFound("User permissions not found")` branch, which on Jellyfin is unreachable. Ferrofin is the correct side. Measured on the F6 pair 2026-08-30, twice: F 204 then GET Users [] then repeat DELETE 404; J 204 then GET Users STILL lists the user then repeat DELETE 204. Discriminating control on the SAME Jellyfin instance: `POST /Playlists/{id}` with `Users: []` (UpdatePlaylist assigns the list wholesale, no List.Remove) DOES clear and persist — so this is not container skew, fixture or a Shares-persistence problem, it is RemoveUserFromShares alone. Previously filed `instance` (instance noise / methodology), which was wrong: a deterministic, twice-reproduced upstream defect is not lab noise. The row cannot reach deep_verified while upstream is broken — journeys.py requires the write's effect on BOTH servers and Jellyfin's legitimately does not hold. That is the correct terminal state for a jellyfin-bug row, not a probe weakness. The second symptom is now recorded rather than asserted: `j_playlist_share` reports the repeat-DELETE status under `notes.playlist_share_repeat_delete_status` in journey-results.json (measured F=404 J=204, twice), deliberately kept OUT of the row's boolean so a future Ferrofin regression to a blind 204 cannot pass by matching Jellyfin.

GET /Albums/{itemId}/Similar.classification: flat-provider methodology (SET-GATED, order not gateable). Seeds of this kind take the C# FLAT provider: one `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [<kind>], EnableGroupByMetadataKey = false, EnableTotalRecordCount = true, OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Ascending)] }` — identical in v10.11.8 (built inline at LibraryController.cs:791-801) and in master (SeriesSimilarItemsProvider.cs:49, MusicAlbumSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, AudioSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, LiveTvProgramSimilarItemsProvider.cs:89). The reads.py leg therefore pins `limit=1000`, far above the fixture's pool, where the answer is the whole candidate set and so fully determined; what is gated there is the SET, TotalRecordCount and every per-item DTO field. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. GREEN BUT VACUOUS ON THE CURRENT FIXTURE — read this row as 'no divergence detected', not as 'verified'. `suite/perf/gen-fixtures.sh` gave each of the 3 albums a UNIQUE music genre, so the candidate universe is empty by construction on BOTH servers and the leg diffs `{"Items": [], "TotalRecordCount": 0}` against itself. A real Ferrofin bug found behind this row IS fixed and verified live: album Genres/Studios/PremiereDate are inherited from the album's Audio children (C# AlbumMetadataService + MetadataService.UpdateGenres/UpdateStudios/UpdatePremiereDate); Ferrofin aggregated only album-artist and year, so every album had `Genres: []` and was unreachable by the Genres= query this endpoint issues. GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Ferrofin returns 0 rows where Jellyfin returns 2. The scorer half is fixed — the seed's kind now selects the C# provider shape (`MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider` is a flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [MusicArtist] }`, and an EMPTY Genres/Tags pair is not a predicate, so an untagged artist must match every other artist; covered by the `an_untagged_artist_seed_still_matches_every_other_artist` unit test). GET /Items/Suggestions.classification: open-work (NOT accepted). `SuggestionsController.GetSuggestions` (v10.11.8 Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/SuggestionsController.cs:78-96) is ONE recursive user query projected with ALL DtoOptions fields, and Ferrofin's handler is a line-for-line port — the handler was never the bug. Random PERMUTES but does not change the set, so at `limit >= |universe|` the answer is fully determined and the probe's seven full-limit legs body-diff it honestly; only the narrow startIndex leg is projected, and only onto what a Random page genuinely determines. The row was red for FIVE independent causes. THREE ARE FIXED HERE. (a) The item-universe gap on its biggest kind: LiveTvProgram was F 0 / J 338 and is now 338/338 (see `GET /Items`). (b) FOUR DTO fields the all-fields projection is supposed to carry and Ferrofin assigned NOWHERE — `RecursiveItemCount` and the folder `UserData.PlayedPercentage`/`Played` (`Folder.FillUserDataDtoValues`, v10.11.8 MediaBrowser.Controller/Entities/Folder.cs:1798-1838, whose two gates are DIFFERENT: the count is gated on its field alone and the played numbers on `SupportsPlayedStatus`, which is why a MusicAlbum carries the count and no percentage); `CumulativeRunTimeTicks` (Emby.Server.Implementations/Dto/DtoService.cs:492-495, the folder branch, not under EnableUserData); `HasLyrics`, unconditional on every Audio DTO and a plain bool — `false`, not an absent key (DtoService.cs:308-311); and `SeriesStudio` for both Episode and Season (:1228-1234 and :1256-1262), which is `series.Studios.FirstOrDefault()` and so lives on a row the projected item is not. (c) The `PresentationUniqueKey` grouping, which the LiveTvProgram mirror made visible: see `GET /Items`. STILL OPEN, both named: the MusicArtist/UserView/Live TV RECORDINGS half of the universe gap, and the BitRate offset — that last one is NOT a Ferrofin defect and is classified on its own row (`GET /Items/{itemId}`, jellyfin-bug: 10.11.8 reports more bitrate than the file physically contains, master's PR #16248 fixed it and Ferrofin ports the fixed form). The remaining Movie 0401/Inception and UserData.LastPlayedDate rows in the current results are LAB DRIFT from other batches' write journeys on this long-lived pair, not defects; they clear on a freshly wiped pair. Previous text kept for the record: open-work (NOT accepted). The old text ('Random, so the set is non-deterministic') was only half true and it hid two real divergences. Random here PERMUTES but does not change the set: `SuggestionsController` runs ONE query (`OrderBy = [(Random, Descending)]`, Recursive, mediaType/type, IsVirtualItem=false) and Ferrofin's handler is a line-for-line port, so at `limit >= |universe|` the answer is fully determined and parity_diff aligns Items by Path. The probe was the problem: `limit=10` sampled 10 of 552 at random and could never diff. It is now eight legs: seven pinned at a full limit (per type), where Random only permutes and the whole body IS diffed, plus one narrow startIndex/limit leg. That narrow leg is the one place a projection is applied — a page of 3 out of 500 Random-ordered rows draws a different triple per call on BOTH servers (measured: three consecutive calls, three different triples each side), so it compares StartIndex, TotalRecordCount and the page length only. Diffing its Items would pin this row red forever and destroy its ability to signal when the two real divergences below are fixed; the projection is scoped to that leg alone and nothing was added to parity_diff.VOLATILE. Two causes remain, BOTH owned by other rows and deliberately left visible here rather than filtered out of the probe: (1) ITEM UNIVERSE — Ferrofin's recursive user-root universe has no MusicArtist, Folder, TvChannel or UserView rows (F 552 vs J 561 unfiltered; per type F 0 vs J 3/3/2/1), the same parentless-by-name/TopParentId cause as GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar; detector `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&limit=100000`, which shows the identical 9-row delta, so it is not this handler's bug. (2) PER-ITEM DTO FIELDS — MediaSources[].Name/Bitrate, MediaStreams[].BitRate (a constant 192000 offset), LocalizedLanguage, Level/IsAVC/Width/Height: the same set already classified on GET /Items/{itemId} as independent-probe noise, inherited here because Suggestions returns full item DTOs. Narrowing the compare to hide either would be the dishonest green; the row stays red until they are fixed on their own rows. The multi-leg probe no longer skips a leg whose servers disagree on status: a status divergence (or a body that is not 200-with-JSON on both sides) is recorded as a mismatch, which is the whole point of keeping the type=MusicArtist and type=TvChannel legs. UNIVERSE GAP, re-measured 2026-08-29 and WIDER than first written: LiveTvProgram belongs on the missing-kind list too — `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=LiveTvProgram` returns 338 rows on Jellyfin and 0 on Ferrofin, while `/LiveTv/Programs` returns the guide on both (F 19200, J 338). The knock-on is visible on a THIRD row: GET /Genres is red only because Jellyfin's genre list carries `News`, the XMLTV guide's programme genre, which Ferrofin's genre list cannot see for the same reason. One fix (give the by-name/programme rows a TopParentId so `scope_to_user_libraries` stops filtering them out) closes /Artists Similar, these Suggestions legs and the /Genres row together; it changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it is its own change WITH the perf gate.

GET /Items/{itemId}.classification: jellyfin-bug (bitrate only): Ferrofin reports MediaStreams[video].BitRate as container-minus-other-streams and MediaSources[].Bitrate as the stream sum; Jellyfin 10.11.8 falls the video stream back to formatInfo.BitRate verbatim (ProbeResultNormalizer.cs:978-987) and then InferTotalBitrate(true) (PRN.cs:259-264), which double-counts the audio. Measured on the fixture: the file is 775053 B / 1.023 s = 6,060,832 bps, so Jellyfin's MediaSources[].Bitrate of 6,253,020 exceeds what the file physically contains, while Ferrofin's 6,061,020 matches ffprobe's own format.bit_rate. Upstream fixed this itself in PR #16248 (master PRN.cs:979-991 comments that formatInfo.BitRate is the container, not the video bitrate) and Ferrofin ports the fixed form. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. GET /Items/Root.classification: accepted-divergence (structural: where the playlists plugin folder hangs). The row's own body diffs CLEAN and this op stays deep-verified — the note records a difference that shows on NEIGHBOURING surfaces, so it is not invisible. Upstream builds TWO roots: the AggregateFolder at `ApplicationPaths.RootFolderPath` and the UserRootFolder at `DefaultUserViewsPath`. `LibraryManager.CreateRootFolder()` (v10.11.8 Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/LibraryManager.cs:838-887) sets `folder.ParentId = rootFolder.Id` where `rootFolder` is the AGGREGATE folder, then `rootFolder.AddVirtualChild(folder)`; the UserRootFolder only picks it up at read time via `GetEligibleChildrenForRecursiveChildren` = `base.Children.ToList()` + `list.AddRange(LibraryManager.RootFolder.VirtualChildren)` (UserRootFolder.cs) — an APPEND, and `UserRootFolder.IsPreSorted => true`, so it is never re-sorted. Ferrofin has no AggregateFolder row and instead stores the playlists folder as a real DB child of the UserRootFolder. That is deliberate: `ChildCount` is served by the grouped child-count query over `ParentId`, so a row that is not a real child is a row the count cannot see — which is the bug this batch fixed (Ferrofin reported 3 where upstream reports 4). TWO OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCES, both measured live on the A4 pair (Ferrofin 18196 / Jellyfin 10.11.8 18197), twice: (1) ORDER on `GET /Items?parentId=<userRootFolderId>` (non-recursive — C# `folder.GetChildren(user, true)`, ItemsController.cs:526-528). Ferrofin sorts the folder inline by SortName: Movies, Music, Playlists, Shows. Jellyfin appends it: Movies, Music, Shows, Playlists. The four items are otherwise identical field-for-field. (2) `ParentId` on the playlists row itself: Ferrofin writes the user root (`e9d5075a…`), Jellyfin writes the aggregate root (`f27caa37…`). Masked in the harness by the pre-existing VOLATILE `ParentId` entry, recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered. NOT an adoption hazard, verified in the C#: on swap-back, Jellyfin's `CreateRootFolder()` sees `!folder.ParentId.Equals(rootFolder.Id)` and repairs the column at startup before serving, and even before that repair the row cannot be double-counted — `Folder.AddChildren` accumulates into a `Dictionary<Guid, BaseItem>` and `GetChildren` returns `result.Values`, so a row reachable both as a DB child and as a VirtualChild collapses to one entry (Folder.cs:1348-1436). ChildCount stays 4 either way. `GET /Library/MediaFolders` — the endpoint jellyfin-web actually uses for this list, and a separately deep-verified row — is UNAFFECTED and matches upstream exactly, including the folder's `CollectionType: playlists` and `CanDelete: false`. Closing this properly means giving Ferrofin a real AggregateFolder row plus a virtual-child seam the count service understands; matching only the ordering would mean special-casing the shared item query on the root parent, which is a perf-gated hot path. Filed as open work, not as an accepted end state.

POST /Items/RemoteSearch/Apply/{itemId}.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Apply itself is correct on both servers; what diverges is whether its effect SURVIVES a library scan. Measured on the lab pair, reproduced three times: Apply into a library with every "Metadata downloaders" box cleared leaves Movie 0497 identical on both (ProductionYear null, Genres [], Studios [], ProviderIds {Tmdb: 603}, and Name / RunTimeTicks / ImageTags / People untouched) - the `unlocked` half of the journey's evidence matches field for field. The journey then runs the library scan to completion on each server and reads the item back again: Jellyfin holds the cleared state, Ferrofin reverts to ProductionYear 2020 / Genres [Comedy, SciFi] / Studios [Ferrofin Studios], re-applied from /media/synth/movies/Movie 0497 (2020)/movie.nfo. That is the whole of the row's `unlocked_after_scan` diff. CAUSE: upstream gates every local metadata reader on a change monitor - v10.11.8 MediaBrowser.XbmcMetadata/Providers/BaseNfoProvider.cs `HasChanged` is `nfoLastWriteTimeUtc - item.DateLastSaved > TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)`, and MetadataService.GetProviders (:613-708) returns an EMPTY provider list when no provider reports a change, so a scan over an item saved more recently than its sidecar runs no providers and merges nothing. Ferrofin's scan re-derives every item from disk on every pass: library_scan.rs calls `fetch_local_nfo` unconditionally for any unlocked row and `save_scanned_items` writes the result over the stored columns. UN-DEFER PATH, and why it is not a ride-along: the port needs three things together - (1) populate `BaseItems.DateLastSaved` on every save (nothing writes it today; the column exists and is bound, but only ever from an entity carrying None), (2) gate `fetch_local_nfo` / `fetch_remote_metadata` on the sidecar-vs-DateLastSaved comparison, and (3) a third scan-upsert variant that PRESERVES the provider-supplied columns when no provider ran, or skipping the read would wipe the very fields it is meant to protect. (1) alone changes `Etag` (dto_service.rs:1260 hashes DateLastSaved) and the `minDateLastSaved` query filters on every DTO in the API, so it is a server-wide change needing its own batch and its own perf run. Recorded here rather than hidden: the journey deliberately forces the scan and waits for it, so this stays a deterministic red instead of a race whose colour depends on when the suite happened to run.

POST /Items/RemoteSearch/MusicArtist.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): the fetcher gate is ported and correct, but Ferrofin cannot RESOLVE a MusicArtist's library, so the gate is inert for that one kind. `LocalProviderManager::remote_search` now runs the C# `CanRefreshMetadata` chain (v10.11.8 ProviderManager.cs:801-830 -> :462-491 -> BaseItemManager.cs:26-46) and resolves the owning library through the reference item's `TopParentId`. Ferrofin's MusicArtist rows are materialized BY NAME out of `ItemValues` (library_scan.rs `item_values_of`, Artist=0/AlbumArtist=1), so they carry TopParentId='', ParentId='', Path=NULL and no `AncestorIds` row — verified directly in the lab DB for all three fixture artists. With no library resolvable the gate falls through permissive, so the GATED leg of the reads probe (ItemId=<own Artist>, IncludeDisabledProviders=false, against a Music library whose TypeOptions[MusicArtist].MetadataFetchers is []) answers with the MusicBrainz hit where Jellyfin answers []. Jellyfin's MusicArtist IS the artist DIRECTORY (measured: Path=/media/synth/music/Artist 01, ParentId=<Music library>), which is what makes `LibraryManager.GetCollectionFolders` (LibraryManager.cs:2262-2303) find the collection folder by path. The UNGATED leg of the same row diffs byte-identical, so the search itself is right; only the reference-item resolution is missing. Fix, in order of faithfulness: (1) give the materialized MusicArtist row its artist directory as `Path` (plus the owning library's TopParentId/ParentId) so the existing resolution works and `/Artists` stops serving Path:null — a library_scan change on the perf-gated path, needing its own batch and its own perf run; or (2) add a path-prefix fallback to `LocalProviderManager::library_options_for`, which only helps once (1) supplies the path. Same root cause as the separately observed `GET /Users/{userId}/Items?IncludeItemTypes=MusicArtist&Recursive=true` returning [] on Ferrofin and 3 on Jellyfin.

GET /Items.classification:
open-work (NOT accepted) — the LiveTvProgram half is PORTED here; what is left is named. Ferrofin never wrote a `BaseItems` row for a Live TV airing: `insert_programs` wrote only `FerrofinLiveTvPrograms` and `program_entity()` built the item in memory at read time for `/LiveTv/Programs` alone, so the recursive item universe held zero airings — measured F 0 / J 338 while `/LiveTv/Programs` answered 338 on BOTH, and `GET /Items/{programId}` was F 404 / J 200. Upstream stores an airing exactly as it stores a channel (`CreateItems(newPrograms, currentChannel, …)` / `UpdateItemsAsync`, v10.11.8 src/Jellyfin.LiveTv/Guide/GuideManager.cs:277-291) and prunes it with the `CleanDatabase(newProgramIdList, [LiveTvProgram])` one line below the channel one (:145-148). `sync_program_items` is that port, on batch G5's channel mechanism rather than beside it: the same bounded field-wise merge (`projection::program_item_update`, so a guide refresh cannot revert a metadata edit on the 24h timer) and the same global clean. Verified live on the lane pair after a `RefreshGuide`: LiveTvProgram F 338 / J 338, `GET /Items/{programId}` 200 on both for the SAME id with ChannelName/ChannelNumber, and `/Genres` picked up the guide-only `News` row it was missing. The stored row now matches the oracle column for column (ParentId=channel, TopParentId=Live TV view, IsVirtualItem=1, UnratedType=LiveTvProgram, MediaType=Unknown, Width/Height=0, ShowId, PresentationUniqueKey NULL). A REGRESSION THIS ROW SHIPPED AND THEN CLOSED, recorded so it cannot come back invisibly: porting the bare `GROUP BY "PresentationUniqueKey"` (upstream's own `dbQuery.GroupBy(e => e.PresentationUniqueKey)`, BaseItemRepository.cs:417) made a KEYLESS row an item-loss bug, because SQLite groups NULLs together. Migration 0027's backfill was scoped `"TopParentId" IS NOT NULL`, and an item-by-name row has TopParentId NULL by construction, so it missed exactly the rows that were keyless: `GET /Items?userId=…&ids=<three Person ids>` measured F 1 / J 3 on the lane pair, and a mixed six-id request returned one item. It also wrote the row's OWN ID as the value, where the five overriding kinds spell it `{Type}-{Name.RemoveDiacritics()}` (Genre.cs:37-47, `Artist` for MusicArtist at MusicArtist.cs:152) — the oracle stores `Person-Bob Parity`, `MusicGenre-Jazz`. Both halves are fixed: migration 0028 widens the scope and narrows the value to the kinds whose key really is their own id, and `ferrofin_db::presentation_key::backfill_by_name_presentation_keys` repairs the five by-name kinds in Rust (SQLite cannot express `RemoveDiacritics`) through the SAME helper the inserts call. Re-measured live after the rebuild: F 3 / J 3 on both routes, mixed six-id F 6, and the lane's stored keys read back `Person-Bob Parity` / `MusicGenre-Jazz`. The probe blind spot that let it through is named too: every leg this batch added to GET /Items is scoped to the recursive user universe, which is the one place TopParentId-less rows are already filtered out, so the guard is the unit test `item_repository::presentation_key_backfill_rescues_a_grouped_query`, not a parity leg.

STILL OPEN on this row. Census re-measured live on the recursive universe after the fix (F total 558 / J 630), every difference named: (1) Live TV RECORDINGS as library items — Jellyfin scans `%AppDataPath%/livetv/recordings` into real rows (measured now: Movie F 500 / J 531, Recording F 0 / J 2); Ferrofin keeps them in `FerrofinLiveTvRecordings` and projects none (`projection::recording_entity`'s doc comment names it). Same mechanism as the programme mirror, third half of the guide. (2) PLAYLISTS: Playlist F 0 / J 25 and ManualPlaylistsFolder F 0 / J 1 — the playlists library and its entries are outside Ferrofin's recursive universe. (3) PHYSICAL FOLDERS beneath each virtual library: Folder F 0 / J 10. Jellyfin materializes the physical folder under every library (`/media/synth/movies`, `/media/synth/music`, `/media/synth/tv`, `/config/data/collections`, `/config/data/livetv/recordings` and the five per-recording folders) as a `Folder` row inside the universe; Ferrofin materializes none. (4) CollectionFolder F 1 / J 0 — the SAME subject as (3) seen from the other side, and NOT lab drift: `/config/data/collections` is a `CollectionFolder` row inside Ferrofin's recursive universe, while on Jellyfin that path is a plain `Folder` and the virtual `Collections` library row itself is excluded. Ferrofin is exposing the library row where upstream exposes its physical child. This was NOT named in the previous version of this row; it is named now. (5) MusicArtist F 0 / J 3 and UserView F 0 / J 1 — the same NULL-`TopParentId` family, different write paths. None of the five is accepted; all five are the next ports on this op.
